articles.title: TradingView webhooks and the 3-second timeout: ACK fast, deliver later
articles.excerpt: TradingView sends alert webhooks as HTTP POST requests to a URL you choose, with the alert message as the body. Its docs are short and strict: "If a remote server takes longer than three seconds to pr…
articles.body: TradingView sends alert webhooks as HTTP POST requests to a URL you choose, with the alert message as the body. Its docs are short and strict: "If a remote server takes longer than three seconds to process a request, the request will be cancelled" ( How to configure webhook alerts ). TradingView resends in one case only: when your server answers with a status between 500 and 599, except 504 . It waits 5 seconds and resends, up to 3 times, so at most 4 sends per trigger ( Webhook resubmission ). It doesn't resend timeouts. A few other limits from the same docs are worth knowing before you debug anything else: Only ports 80 and 443 are accepted. IPv6 isn't supported, so your hostname needs an IPv4 (A) record.

articles.title: SMS OTP Login: How a Node.js Backend Sends and Verifies Airline Codes
articles.excerpt: SMS OTP gets an airline disruption-alert login shipped quickly, but the hosted verify call is only half the system. Pick a managed OTP product, then own cooldowns, IP and device limits, country policy…
articles.body: SMS OTP gets an airline disruption-alert login shipped quickly, but the hosted verify call is only half the system. Pick a managed OTP product, then own cooldowns, IP and device limits, country policy, retries, and delivery evidence in the application. Otherwise a delayed message looks like a bad code, a retry can become an SMS burst, and an attacker can turn the login form into a sending tool. Short answer: use the provider's send and verify operations for token lifecycle, keep abuse decisions before the send, retry only transient failures, and poll delivery state when the provider has no webhook. This is the practical beginner path. It also leaves an audit trail that can answer who requested a code, which policy allowed it, what the provider returned, and whether delivery progressed.

articles.body: A note for dev.to readers: these tools use pdf-lib to edit files, pdf.js to render pages, and qpdf compiled to WebAssembly for AES-256 encryption, all running client-side. Nothing is uploaded. Contracts, bank statements, payslips, medical letters, ID scans: the PDFs we most often need to merge, shrink or lock are also the ones we least want to hand to a stranger. Yet the usual way to do it online is to upload the file to a website, let its server process it, and download the result. This guide explains what that actually involves, and how to do the same jobs without your file ever leaving your computer. What happens when you "upload" a PDF A typical online PDF tool copies your document to its server, works on it there, and keeps the result long enough for you to download it.

articles.title: Windows Event ID 37 Doesn't Mean Your CPU Is Overheating
articles.excerpt: I build a small Windows diagnostic tool. One of its rules looked at the System event log, found Kernel-Processor-Power Event ID 37, and told the user: "your cooling system is probably the problem." Th…
articles.body: I build a small Windows diagnostic tool. One of its rules looked at the System event log, found Kernel-Processor-Power Event ID 37, and told the user: "your cooling system is probably the problem." Then I ran it on my own PC, which has no cooling problem. It told me my cooling was the problem. This post is about why Event 37 is a terrible proxy for overheating, and the three filters that fixed the false positive. What Event 37 actually says Event ID 37 from Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Processor-Power reads roughly: the speed of processor N is being limited by system firmware. Heat is one reason firmware does that. It is not the only one. A power limit, a weak charger, a battery state or an OEM power profile produce the same event. The event tells you a limit was applied.

articles.title: Solving the Text Replacement Headache in AI Generated Images
articles.excerpt: AI image generation has evolved rapidly, but anyone who has worked with it knows the pain: text consistency in images remains a huge challenge. Whether it's typos in poster designs, unwanted artifacts…
articles.body: AI image generation has evolved rapidly, but anyone who has worked with it knows the pain: text consistency in images remains a huge challenge . Whether it's typos in poster designs, unwanted artifacts on product labels, or translated text looking messy, traditional re-generation often ruins the original composition. The Real Problem with Text Editing in Images When building workflows around modern image generation APIs (like fal.ai), standard diffusion models frequently hallucinate typography. If you just want to fix a single misspelling or change a brand slogan, running a full prompt re-roll can alter the entire background layout. To solve this efficiently, a practical workflow requires: Precise Inpainting & Masking : Isolate the typo zone without touching surrounding graphics.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 12, 1964: The Soviet Union launches Voskhod 1, the 1st multi-person cosmonaut crew, into space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight . This was the first time that a spacecraft carried more than one person into orbit, with three cosmonauts packed inside the spacecraft. Only two cosmonauts were originally supposed to fly on this mission, but Soviet politicians pressured the Russian space program to add one more. This left no room for spacesuits on board, so this also became the first spaceflight without spacesuits . Two of the crewmembers, an engineer and a doctor, became the first civilians to go to space. On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched the first multiperson mission, Voskhod 1, which launched three Russian cosmonauts into space.

articles.title: What caused a mysterious atmospheric explosion in Siberia in 1908?
articles.excerpt: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history.
articles.body: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history. That day, at approximately 7:15 a.m. local time, observers in Siberia's remote Tunguska region became witnesses to the entry of a brilliant fireball into Earth's atmosphere , trailing smoke across the dawn sky and culminating in a flash brighter than the sun itself. Within seconds, the explosion and resulting shock waves that followed reportedly knocked some members of the nearby Indigenous Evenki population off their feet, and caused damage to dwellings and livestock, while seismic instruments hundreds of miles away logged tremors caused by the blast.

articles.body: If you're driving through GM's sprawling campus in Warren, Michigan, you'd likely ignore the pair of adjacent, anonymous white buildings tucked away in the upper reaches of the 710-acre space. Inside those buildings, which total half a million square feet together, is a massive construction project that's still in progress. Once completed, it will house GM's new Battery Cell Development Center, where the automaker is working furiously to build new prototype cells with the goal of slashing the cost of its EVs. articles.title: UAE unveils lander for bold 7-asteroid mission set to launch in 2028 (photos)
articles.excerpt: In March 2028, the UAE is set to launch an ambitious mission to the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter that will culminate with a landing attempt on a mysteriously reddish space rock.
articles.body: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has moved a step closer to launching its second-ever interplanetary mission — an ambitious, eight-year exploration of seven asteroids between Mars and Jupiter that will culminate with a landing on the mysteriously red asteroid 269 Justitia. The mission team unveiled a half-scale model of the homegrown probe that will make that landing during an Oct. 1 press conference in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE. The autonomous craft will ride attached to the main spacecraft MBR Explorer , named after Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the ruler of Dubai and the UAE's prime minister.
